properties.address: 30 N W Circus Pl, Edinburgh EH3 6TP, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation composed of Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock belonging to the Strathclyde Group, overlain by dense glacial lodgement till and boulder clay descending toward the Water of Leith basin. Masonry lithics consist primarily of pale cream-to-buff Craigleith and grey Hailes quartz-rich sandstone, characterized by high silica content, cross-bedding, and exceptional weathering resistance. Bedding joints set in traditional hydraulic lime and sharp river sand mortars. Roadway sub-base capped by olivine-dolerite (whinstone) setts and dressed Scottish granite kerbstones.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Urban dendrological specimens consisting of *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm). Date-grounded December 25 winter state: complete deciduous dormancy, total defoliation, exposing complex architecture of bare structural limbs, rugged grey-brown bark, and intricate branch tracery.

properties.architectural_summary: Georgian Neoclassical multi-storey residential and commercial tenement terraces descending along a continuous gradient. Four-storey over basement ashlar facades with planarized vertical load-bearing lines. Ground floors exhibit channelled ashlar rustication and integrated 19th-century timber shopfront fascias; upper storeys display polished ashlar with crisp broached margins. Fenestration arranged in uniform vertical grids of timber-framed 12-pane and 6-over-6 sash-and-case windows with deep stone reveals. Rooflines defined by continuous moulded eaves cornices, blocking courses, pitched Scotch slate timber-framed roofs, pitched dormer projections, and substantial ashlar chimney stacks with clay chimney pots. Drop-light basement areas bounded by vertical wrought-iron spearhead railings.
